titleStmt.title: New bounds on the cardinality of Hausdorff spaces and regular spaces
titleStmt.author: Carlson

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: New bounds on the cardinality of Hausdorff spaces and regular spaces

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Using weaker versions of the cardinal function ψc(X), we derive a series of new bounds for the cardinality of Hausdorff spaces and regular spaces that do not involve ψc(X) nor its variants at all.

span.label: cardinality bounds for Hausdorff and regular spaces
span.quote: Many bounds on the cardinality of a topological space X involve the pseudocharacter cardinal function, ψ(X), or its variant, the closed pseudocharacter ψc(X).

span.label: mathematical-proof
span.quote: As their proofs rely on sophisticated closing-off arguments, these results are deemed “difficult” in the sense of Hodel [15], section 4.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: bounding |X| by the family of regular open sets and then bounding that family by a closing-off argument on density, so the pseudocharacter can be weakened without loss
span.quote: This is achieved by establishing that |X| ≤ |RO(X)|wψc(X), where RO(X) is the collection of regular open subsets of X, and, using a modified version of Sun’s closing-off argument, that d(X) ≤ πχ(X)c(X)dψc(X) for any Hausdorff space X.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: constructing an injection of the space into a family of small subsets indexed by weak closed pseudobases, which transfers existing bounds from ψc(X) to wψc(X)
span.quote: Using one-to-one map arguments, we can replace ψc(X) with wψc(X) in other cardinality bounds.

span.label: Whether the wψc-based bound holds for compact homogeneous Hausdorff spaces is left unresolved by the paper's own examples.
span.quote: However, even given Examples 3.11 and 5.1 it is still unclear whether 2wψc(X) is a bound for the cardinality of all compact, homogeneous Hausdorff spaces.

span.label: The corresponding bound for general (non-quasiregular) Hausdorff spaces is posed as an open question rather than proved.
span.quote: Question 4.8. If X is Hausdorff, is |X| ≤ 2c(X)πχ(X)ot(X)?

span.label: No separation axiom is assumed anywhere, so every result's hypotheses have to be read locally rather than inherited from the word 'space'.
span.note: what this limits: any theorem quoted from this paper as being about 'a space': the author makes no global assumption of any separation axiom, so the hypotheses stated in each individual result are the only ones in force
span.quote: We make no global assumptions of any separation axiom on a topological space in this paper

span.label: The novelty claim for the central new bound is hedged, and the hedge is the author's.
span.note: what this limits: the priority of the bound on cardinality by density and weak closed pseudocharacter: the author says it appears to be new in the literature rather than asserting it is, and notes a related result was already known for regular spaces
span.quote: The latter result appears to be new in the literature even when wψc(X) is replaced with ψc(X), although it was known that |X| ≤ 2d(X)ψ(X) if X is regular

span.label: Two theorems reach the same kind of conclusion by different sophisticated arguments and the author cannot unify them.
span.note: what this limits: treating the two density bounds here as one result: the author states the proofs are different sophisticated closing-off arguments and asks, as an open question, whether a common proof exists
span.quote: The proofs are sophisticated closing-off arguments, but different. We ask the following: Question 3.3. Is there a common proof of Theorems 3.1 and 3.2

span.label: The substitution the paper's new functions permit is shown not to extend to the compact case.
span.note: what this limits: generalising the replacement of pseudocharacter by the new weaker functions: compact examples are given showing the substitution fails in the classical bound for the cardinality of a compact Hausdorff space
span.quote: Compact examples show that ψ(X) cannot be replaced with dψc(X)wψc(X) in the bound 2ψ(X) for the cardinality of a compact Hausdorff space X

span.label: separation axiom
span.quote: We make no global assumptions of any separation axiom on a topological space in this paper

span.label: closing-off argument
span.quote: The proofs are sophisticated closing-off arguments, but different

span.label: difficult
span.quote: As their proofs rely on sophisticated closing-off arguments, these results are deemed “difficult” in the sense of Hodel

span.label: pseudocharacter
span.quote: Many bounds on the cardinality of a topological space X involve the pseudocharacter cardinal function

span.label: cardinal function
span.quote: In this study we introduce two cardinal functions for a Hausdorff space X that are weaker than the closed pseudocharacter

span.label: 'space' - WITH NO SEPARATION AXIOM ATTACHED: in much of the topology literature the bare word silently carries Hausdorff or regular or T1 depending on the author, so this paper states that it assumes none of them globally and every hypothesis is local to its theorem
span.quote: We make no global assumptions of any separation axiom on a topological space in this paper

span.label: 'difficult' - A CLASSIFICATION OF PROOF TECHNIQUE, ATTRIBUTED: the word is scare-quoted and referred to a particular author and section, and what earns it is that the proofs rely on sophisticated closing-off arguments, not that the statements are hard to understand
span.quote: As their proofs rely on sophisticated closing-off arguments, these results are deemed “difficult” in the sense of Hodel

span.label: pseudocharacter and closed pseudocharacter - THE SAME NUMBER ONLY UNDER A HYPOTHESIS: they are ordered for any Hausdorff space and become equal when the space is regular, so whether a bound stated with one is a bound stated with the other depends on a separation axiom
span.quote: It is clear that ψ(X) ≤ ψc(X) ≤ χ(X) for any Hausdorff space X. Furthermore, if X is regular, it can be seen that ψ(X) = ψc(X)

span.label: extends → the cardinality bounds of Šapirovskiĭ [22] and Sun [23]
span.quote: We improve the results of ˇSapirovski˘ı and Sun by showing |X| ≤ πχ(X)c(X)wψc(X) if X is regular, and |X| ≤ πχ(X)c(X)dψc(X)wψc(X) if X is Hausdorff.

span.label: extends → Gotchev, Tkachenko and Tkachuk's bound πw(X)ot(X)ψc(X) [13]
span.quote: We show in the next result that ψc(X) can be replaced with wψc(X).

span.label: extends → the Bella-Cammaroto bound d(X)t(X)ψc(X) [1] as improved by the author in [6]
span.quote: We show in Theorem 4.17 that in fact ψc(X) can further be replaced with wψc(X).

span.label: difficult —operationalised-as→ closing-off argument
span.quote: As their proofs rely on sophisticated closing-off arguments, these results are deemed “difficult” in the sense of Hodel

span.label: cardinal function —contrasted-with→ pseudocharacter
span.quote: In this study we introduce two cardinal functions for a Hausdorff space X that are weaker than the closed pseudocharacter

span.label: For a quasiregular Hausdorff space the cardinality is bounded by πχ(X)^(c(X)wψc(X)), which strengthens Šapirovskiĭ's classical bound by replacing the pseudocharacter with the weak closed pseudocharacter.
span.quote: Theorem 3.9. If X is quasiregular and Hausdorff then |X| ≤ πχ(X)c(X)wψc(X).

span.label: For any Hausdorff space the cardinality is bounded by πχ(X)^(c(X)dψc(X)wψc(X)), improving Sun's bound by splitting the closed pseudocharacter into its dense and weak parts.
span.quote: Theorem 3.10. If X is Hausdorff then |X| ≤ πχ(X)c(X)dψc(X)wψc(X).

span.label: Every Hausdorff space satisfies |X| ≤ 2^(d(X)wψc(X)), a bound the author reports as new even in the stronger form with the ordinary closed pseudocharacter.
span.quote: Theorem 4.9. If X is Hausdorff then |X| ≤ 2d(X)wψc(X).

span.label: The density of an arbitrary Hausdorff space is bounded by πχ(X)^(c(X)dψc(X)), extending to Hausdorff spaces a density bound previously known only for regular or quasiregular spaces.
span.quote: Theorem 3.2. If X is Hausdorff then d(X) ≤ πχ(X)c(X)dψc(X).

span.label: The cardinality of a Hausdorff space is bounded by the number of its regular open sets raised to the weak closed pseudocharacter, which is the lemma underpinning most of the paper's new bounds.
span.quote: Proposition 3.8. If X is Hausdorff, then |X| ≤ |RO(X)|wψc(X).

span.label: Compact examples with countable dψc(X)wψc(X) but arbitrarily large cardinality show the product dψc(X)wψc(X) cannot substitute for the pseudocharacter in the classical bound 2^ψ(X) for compact Hausdorff spaces.
span.quote: Compact examples show that ψ(X) cannot be replaced with dψc(X)wψc(X) in the bound 2ψ(X) for the cardinality of a compact Hausdorff space X.

span.label: A quasiregular Hausdorff space whose cellularity is at most the continuum and whose π-character is countable has at most 2^c points.
span.quote: It follows from Corollary 4.6(3) that a quasiregular Hausdorff space with cellularity at most c and countable π-character has cardinality at most 2c.

span.label: The Bella–Cammaroto-type bound d(X)^(t(X)ψc(X)) can be sharpened for Hausdorff spaces to d(X)^(wt(X)wψc(X)), weakening both tightness and closed pseudocharacter simultaneously.
span.quote: Theorem 4.17. If X is Hausdorff then |X| ≤ d(X)wt(X)wψc(X).

span.label: In a homogeneous Hausdorff space the new dense closed pseudocharacter collapses to the ordinary closed pseudocharacter, so it yields no improvement there.
span.quote: Thus if X is homogeneous and Hausdorff we have dψc(X) = ψc(X).

span.label: σ-compact homogeneous spaces of arbitrarily large cardinality with wψc(X) ≤ c show that 2^wψc(X) fails as a cardinality bound for that class.
span.quote: Therefore, 2wψc(X) is not a bound for the cardinality of all σ- compact homogeneous spaces.

span.label: weak closed pseudocharacter wψc(X)
span.quote: We define wψc(x, X) to be the least infinite cardinal κ such that x has a weak closed pseudobase of cardinality κ. The weak closed pseudocharacter wψc(X) is defined as wψc(X) = sup{wψc(x, X) : x ∈ X}.

span.label: dense closed pseudocharacter dψc(X)
span.quote: The dense closed pseudocharacter dψc(X) of X is defined as the least infinite cardinal κ such that X has a dense set D such that ψc(d, X) ≤ κ for every d ∈ D.

span.label: quasiregular space
span.quote: A space X is quasiregular if every nonempty open set contains a nonempty regular closed set.

span.label: homogeneous space
span.quote: A space X is homogeneous if for every pair of points x and y in X there exists a homeomorphism h : X → X such that h(x) = y.

span.label: C-saturated subset
span.quote: Given a cover C of X, a subset A ⊆ X is C-saturated if A ∩ C is dense in A for every C ∈ C. It is clear that the union of C-saturated subsets is C-saturated.

span.label: weak tightness wt(X)
span.quote: The weak tightness wt(X) of a space X is defined as the least infinite cardinal κ for which there is a cover C of X such that |C| ≤ 2κ and for every C ∈ C, t(C) ≤ κ and X = cl2κC.

span.label: regular open set
span.quote: A subset of X is regular open if it is of the form intU where U is open. Let RO(X) denote the set of regular open sets.
